title: What Happens to Bank Accounts When Someone Passes Away Without a Will
bigPicture: When a person dies without a will, the bank follows state rules to decide who receives the money in their accounts.
whatYouNeedToKnow: The bank will freeze the account until it receives legal proof of who is entitled to the funds.
State law usually gives the money to the closest living relatives, such as a spouse, children, or parents.
If no relatives can be found, the money may go to the state after a certain period.
commonMistakesToAvoid: Assuming the bank will automatically give the money to a friend or caregiver.
Trying to withdraw money from the account without proper legal authority.
actionSteps: Contact the bank as soon as possible and ask what documents they need to release the funds.
Gather any available identification, death certificate, and proof of relationship to the deceased to show the bank.
